description.narrative: Den föreslagna påfyllnaden av Zim-fonden om 20 MSEK kommer att bidra till att den avslutande delen av projektets fas 2 kommer att till en större del finansieras. Danmark fyller på fonden med ca 19 MUSD och Sverige i o m den föreslagna påfyllnaden ca 3 MUSD. AfDB/MMU har initialt föreslagit för Project Oversight Committee (POC) att använda tillgänglig finansiering till att fullfinansiera hela projektet avseende vatten & sanitet phase 2 (stage 1 och 2), och låta elektrifieringsprojektet agera dragspel där resterande medel (knappa 3 MUSD) används för prioriterade insatser inom EPIRP phase 2. Eventuella ytterligare givarmedel får då allokeras till EPIRP upp till den budgeterade nivån om 17,5 MUSD för den avslutande fas 2 av EPIRP. Slutligt beslut om fördelning av tillgängliga medel i fas 2 avses tas först vid fondens styrelsemöte (Project Oversight Committee, POC) i december 2014 och bekräftas i samband med AfDBs nästa styrelsemöte (ca februari 2015). Urgent Water Supply and Sanitation Rahabilitation Project (UWSSRP) phase 2 avser färdigställa påbörjade rehabiliteringsarbeten av vatten- och sanitetsanläggningar i Harare, Ruwa, Chitungwiza och Redcliff. Projektet inkluderar arbete för förändrade beteenden avseende hygien, kapacitetesbyggande (bla utarbetande av investeringsplaner, utbildning) samt projektadministration. Emergency Power Infrastructure Rehabilitation Project (EPIRP) phase 2 planerar med en begränsad finansiering arbeta med miljöåtgärder avseende Hwange Power Plant.
Multi-Donor Trust Fund administered by the African Development Bank for funding of projects for rehabilitation of water supply and sanitation services and the electric power sector.

UWSSRP:Impact objective: Improved quality of life. Outcome objective: 1. Improved availability of water supply in the project areas. 2. Raw sewage removed from residential areas and treatment capacity increased.3. Financial sustainability and performance of sector in the project areas improved. EPIRP:Impact objective: The power production capability of the installed capacity fully restored with due attention to environmental safety & protection. Outcome objective:1. Access to reliable electricity supply2. Improved environmental quality at Hwange Power Plant and surroundings.

description.narrative:
ZimFund was an emergency program established in 2010, to contribute to early recovery and development efforts in Zimbabwe by mobilizing donor resources and promoting donor coordination in the country, to channel financial assistance to such efforts. The ZimFund donor countries are Australia, Denmark, Germany, Norway, Switzerland, Sweden, and the United Kingdom. The donors contributed a total of US$145.8 million. The ZimFund account earned an interest and income of US$2.97 million, bringing the total amount of ZimFund resources to US$148.77 million. The project had two components, the Urgent Water Supply and Sanitation Rehabilitation (UWSSRP) and the Emergency Power Infrastructure Rehabilitation Project (EPIRP) that were both implemented in two phases each. The project was implemented by the African Development Bank (AfDB).
Among its key achievements, the UWSSRP implemented in six (6) municipalities managed to have:
- 6 water treatment works rehabilitated - 12 clean water pump units replaced - Raw water pumping units replaced - 1 water reservoir built - 9 wastewater treatment works rehabilitated/replaced - 13 wastewater effluent pumping units rehabilitated/replaced - 28 raw sewage pumping units rehabilitated/replaced - 12.5 km of new trunk sewer constructed - 6 pieces of sewer cleaning equipment handed over to municipalities - 80 community WASH groups trained - 116 school WASH groups trained - 190 municipal operations and maintenance staff trained - 6 municipal revenue and cost recovery strategies prepared
- 78 km of water distribution system rehabilitated. - 15 water pumping stations rehabilitated. - 27 km of sewage reticulation system replaced.
The project achieved results above its targets. A total of 2 056 906 (or 103 %) of targeted people benefited from the projects rehabilitated water infrastructure through improved periodic access to water. There was 500 % (or 5.4 times more than expected) of targeted Non-Revenue Water (NRW) levels reduction in five of the municipalities except for the City of Harare, where NRW remained at 65 % levels at the closure of the project.
Under the EPIRP component of the project, the following was achieved by the project:
- 7 transmission transformers installed - 507 distribution transformers installed throughout the country - 16 sub-transmission circuit breakers replaced - A combined 360 km of cable and overhead lines replaced throughout the country - Electrical energy production at Hwange Power Station improved from 3,133 GWh to 3,850 GWh - Over 529 768 people in residential areas had their sewage reticulation powered by reliable power - 11 632 customers restored to the network - 11 097 customers added to the network
The EPIRP component also saw the rehabilitated transmission and distribution networks (repaired and replaced cables, overhead lines, and transformers and their related accessories). A 175 MVA transformer was installed at the Bulawayo substation. The transformer has the capacity to supply 175 000 customers in Bulawayo and nearby towns. Another 75MVA132/36kV transformer was delivered at Orange Grove substation in Mutare. Dust suppression equipment was supplied for the Hwange Ash Dam. This consisted of a dump truck, a pipe carrier, excavators and 2 ride on compactors, among other accompanying equipment.
